title: Per-tenant grace-period adaptive cutover and fallback regulator
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Global fallback policies aggressively cut over tenants as soon as cluster-level 429/timeouts spike, causing noisy throttles for a few noisy tenants and unnecessary model variant evictions. Goal: Implement a per-tenant 'grace period' regulator that combines recent error-rate signals, token-rate spikes, and probe results to decide whether to trigger immediate fallback, gradual cutover, or probationary throttling. The regulator should be tenant-scoped, configurable via routing policy, and interoperable with regional/tier routing and existing circuit-breaker systems.

Acceptance criteria:
- New regulator evaluates per-tenant windowed metrics (60s/5m) and outputs one of: PASS, PROBATION, SOFT-FALLBACK, HARD-FALLBACK.
- Integrates with existing routing controller so decisions are enforced within 200ms of state transition.
- Telemetry: emit tenant decision events with contributing signals and a decision score.
- Can be toggled per-customer via routing policy and supports safe rollout (canary by tenant ID set).
- Automated tests for decision boundaries and end-to-end canary in staging.

Design notes:
- Signals: 429 rate, upstream timeout rate, 5xx error rate, median latency, request-per-second delta, recent probe success rate to model variants.
- Decision model: weighted scoring engine with hysteresis and exponential backoff for repeated transitions. Default weights tuned conservatively; PM/SE can adjust via config.
- Grace period semantics: when a tenant crosses the soft threshold, start a grace timer (default 30s). If errors persist beyond grace, escalate to probation or soft-fallback. If errors abate, decay score over a configurable half-life.
- Probe flow: before a hard-fallback we will perform a fast compatibility probe to fallback model variant; only commit hard fallback if probe fails or probe indicates latency improvement >20%.
- Integration: regulator runs inside routing controller as a tenant-scoped decision layer; outputs are persisted to distributed state so multiple routing proxies read consistent view.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype scoring function and local integration test harness (2d)
2) Add telemetry events + metrics (latency, decision_count, avg_score) (3d)
3) Implement grace-timer + hysteresis in routing controller (4d)
4) Probe orchestration and safety checks (3d)
5) Staging canary with 10 low-traffic tenants for 48h (2d)
6) Rollout gradual enable-by-customer (automated flag)

Metrics to monitor post-rollout:
- False-positive fallback rate (fallbacks where latency/error improved within 60s)
- Customer error rate reduction (change before/after)
- Fallback duration distribution
- Model-variant probe success ratio

Risk and trade-offs:
- Memory/CPU: per-tenant windows add state; mitigate with LRU eviction and default TTL.
- Complexity: added decision layer increases operational surface area. Start with conservative defaults and feature-flag rollout.
- Telemetry volume: decision events can be verbose; batch and sample for low-traffic tenants.
